focus: weighted interpolation, factorization, ramification cleanup, and characteristic-safe propagation

messages.body_markdown: Can the incidence roadmap expose an $(\epsilon,a)$-core as in AE-03 and ensure that any selected $T'\subseteq T$ retains all core edges incident to each selected line? AE-18--AE-20 need the inherited lower bound $\deg_G(L)\ge k$; a universal smaller reaching family is ruled out by AE-14, so a decode alternative must accompany sparsification.
messages.subject: Whole-line core handoff

messages.body_markdown: AE-21 suggests a way around the $p^{-1/2}$ component-mixing floor. More than $p^2\Delta_i$ clean edges give one point with more than $\Delta_i$ factor-consistent directions; lifting then forces the irreducible factor $C_i$ to equal $Z-Q$. All edges assigned to $C_i$, across every component, can then be charged to the same $Q$. Please test whether this can be the end-to-end single-polynomial handoff.
messages.subject: Vinh-free factor aggregation

messages.body_markdown: Warning: the accepted whole-explainer chain has $D\asymp\sqrt{d\tau p^2/k}$ and requires $D<k$; together with $\tau\ge k/(4p)$ it has a square-root floor. Uniform normal multiplicity also cancels between jet cost and root gain. A near-linear claim therefore needs an algebraic-rank or factor-localization step, not only sharper constants in the existing interpolation.
messages.subject: Whole-explainer floor

messages.body_markdown: The factorwise polar bound in AE-17 is currently supported only by pending researcher-0007 steps. An independent proof audit of the weighted resultant multiplicity $\Xi_i$ and help with AE-19's heavy-factor versus cross-factor-decoder dichotomy would be especially valuable.
messages.subject: Audit factorwise localization

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence instance
nodes.notes: This fixes only the bivariate prime-field campaign regime.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and polynomials $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$ for all affine lines $L$. Define $$\mathcal I=\{(x,L):x\in L\text{ and }P_L(x)=f(x)\},\qquad \mu(E)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}$$ for $E\subseteq\mathcal I$.

nodes.label: Weighted graph relations
nodes.notes: The restriction map is the Lean-level object whose rank must eventually be controlled.
nodes.statement_markdown: Give $X,Y,Z$ weights $1,1,d$. Let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}(A)\le D\},\qquad N_d(D)=\dim V_D=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor D/d\rfloor}\binom{D-dj+2}{2}.$$ For an affine parametrization $L(t)$, put $\rho_L(A)=A(L(t),P_L(t))$. A graph relation on $T$ is a nonzero $A$ satisfying $\rho_L(A)=0$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Algebra-ready core
nodes.notes: This is the interface expected from popularity pruning or the incidence roadmap.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For $0<\epsilon\le1$ and $a>0$, an $(\epsilon,a)$-core is an accepted subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$ with $$\mu(E)\ge a\epsilon,
\qquad
\min_{v\in X\sqcup T}\deg_G(v)\ge k:=\lfloor a\epsilon p\rfloor.$$

nodes.label: Constant-loss core pruning
nodes.notes: The cited step was individually judged valid, but its enclosing exact audit verdict is revise, so this import remains provisional.
nodes.statement_markdown: If the full accepted graph has mass $\epsilon$, then it has a subgraph of mass at least $\epsilon/4$ and minimum degree at least $\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$; in particular it contains an $(\epsilon,1/100)$-core.

nodes.label: Component measures
nodes.notes: This begins the exact accepted component-sensitive backbone.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a connected accepted subgraph of minimum degree $k$, put $t=|T|$ and $\tau=t/[p(p+1)]$, and let $C_*=2^{40}$. If $$k^2\ge C_*dp,
\qquad
k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\frac{|X|}{p^2}\ge\frac{k}{4p},
\qquad
\tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Component-sensitive reaching family
nodes.notes: Distinct points of one target line depend on disjoint other-line choices.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under AE-05, there is $R\subseteq T$ such that, with $r=|R|$, $$\frac{4t}{k}\le r\le\frac{16t}{k},$$ and more than half of the accepted neighbors of every $L\in T$ are incident to a line of $R\setminus\{L\}$. Moreover $r\ge p+1$.

nodes.label: Weighted squarefree interpolant
nodes.notes: This is ordinary, not multiplicity, interpolation.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Set $$D=16\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{dr}\right\rfloor+1\right).$$ There is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ with $A_Z\ne0$ and $\rho_M(A)=0$ for every $M\in R$. Furthermore, $$D^2\le\frac{32768d\tau p^2}{k},
\qquad
\frac Dk<\frac1{5000},
\qquad
D<k\le p<r.$$

nodes.label: Linewise identity extension
nodes.notes: The root count is lossless but consumes the full weighted degree $D$.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, $$\rho_L(A)=A(L(t),P_L(t))=0.$$

nodes.label: Content and resultant cleanup
nodes.notes: The use of a coprime directional derivative is characteristic-safe and avoids discriminants.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient gcd in $Z$. Then $B$ is squarefree, $\deg B<p$, and there is a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1$. After deleting at most $D$ content lines, at most $D(D-1)$ identically degenerate lines, and at most $D$ bad accepted points on every remaining line, the exceptional edge set satisfies $$|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$

nodes.label: Surviving clean core
nodes.notes: Connectivity may fragment during this peeling.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under AE-05--AE-09, $$\frac{|E_{\mathrm{exc}}|}{|E|}\le\frac Dk+\frac{16384dp}{k^2}<\frac1{4000}.$$ Peeling vertices of degree below $k_1=\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ leaves a nonempty accepted subgraph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $k_1$.

nodes.label: Vertical simplicity from two directions
nodes.notes: Two distinct retained lines through a point give independent directions because the base dimension is exactly two.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every point vertex $x$ of $G_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad
B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component decoder
nodes.notes: Newton lifting divides only by certified nonzero values of $B_Z$ and produces one polynomial, not a list.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under AE-05--AE-11, there is a single $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Whole-explainer square-root floor
nodes.notes: This diagnoses the accepted architecture; it is not an impossibility theorem for other algebraic methods.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Within AE-05--AE-12, $$D=\Theta\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{d\tau p^2}{k}}\right),
\qquad
D<k,$$ so $k^3=\Omega(d\tau p^2)$. Since $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, this entails $k^2=\Omega(dp)$. Thus $k=\Theta(\epsilon p)$ cannot close this whole-explainer route below $\epsilon=\Omega((d/p)^{1/2})$.

nodes.label: Universal-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: The easy constant decoder forces any improved selector statement to be a sparsify-or-decode dichotomy.
nodes.statement_markdown: For suitable integers $K$ there are legal constant-label tables with $1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$ such that every line family reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while some constant polynomial $Q$ satisfies $\Pr[Q=f]\ge\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Uniform-jet interpolation barrier
nodes.notes: This citation is provisional: its audit requires integer quantifiers and restricts asymptotic codimension claims to the raw-feasible regime.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $s,D$ be integers with $s\ge1$ and $d\le D<p$. For $n>D$, define $$C_s(D,d)=\sum_{a+b<s}\max(D-a-db+1,0).$$ If raw dimension counting gives $N_d(D)>nC_s(D,d)$ and transfer uses $h$ compatible intersections with $sh>D$, then $$h^2>\frac{dn}{12}.$$

nodes.label: Factor allocation and polar data
nodes.notes: Allocation is possible because each product restriction vanishes in the integral domain $\mathbb F_p[t]$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $B=c\prod_{i=1}^sC_i$ be primitive and squarefree with irreducible $Z$-dependent factors. Allocate each line satisfying $B(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ to one factor satisfying $C_i(L(t),P_L(t))=0$, obtaining $T=\bigsqcup_iT_i$. Put $$E_i=\{(x,L)\in E:L\in T_i\},
\quad
\mu_i=\mu(E_i),
\quad
\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i),
\quad
r_i=\deg_Z(C_i),
\quad
\gamma_i=\operatorname{wdeg}(C_{i,Z}),$$ and $$\Xi_i=(r_i-1)\Delta_i+r_i\gamma_i-dr_i(r_i-1).$$

nodes.label: Factorwise separability and polar bound
nodes.notes: The source audit is pending. The sufficient characteristic condition $\Delta_i<p$ may later be weakened to $\deg_Z(C_i)<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Assume $\operatorname{wdeg}(B)<p$. Then $\gcd(C_i,C_{i,Z})=1$. For each $i$, at most $\Xi_i$ lines of $T_i$ satisfy $C_{i,Z}(L(t),P_L(t))=0$ identically, and every other assigned line has total polar-zero multiplicity at most $\gamma_i$. Hence the normalized ramified-incidence loss is at most $$\sum_i\frac{\min\{|T_i|,\Xi_i\}}{p(p+1)}+
\sum_i\frac{|T_i|\gamma_i}{p^2(p+1)}.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear weighted-rank dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the main interpolation gap. AE-14 rules out an incidence-only proof of the relation branch.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\eta<1$ there are constants $C_\eta,A_\eta,a_\eta>0$ such that the following holds. If $G$ is an $(\epsilon,a_\eta)$-core and $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac d p\right)^{1-\eta},$$ then either one polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfies $\Pr[Q=f]\ge a_\eta\epsilon$, or there are $T'\subseteq T$, $E'=E\cap(X\times T')$, and a squarefree primitive graph relation $B$ of positive $Z$-degree such that $$\mu(E')\ge a_\eta\epsilon,
\qquad
B(L(t),P_L(t))=0\quad(L\in T'),$$ and, for $D=\operatorname{wdeg}(B)$ and $k=\lfloor a_\eta\epsilon p\rfloor$, $$D\le A_\eta d\epsilon^{-\eta/(1-\eta)}<\frac{k}{8}<p.$$

nodes.label: Heavy factor or cross-factor decoder
nodes.notes: This is the central factor-consistency and list-to-single-polynomial gap. A plausible route charges changes of assigned factor through pairwise $Z$-resultants.
nodes.statement_markdown:
There is $b_\eta>0$ such that every relation alternative in AE-18 has one of the following outcomes: a polynomial $Q$ of total degree at most $d$ with $\Pr[Q=f]\ge b_\eta\epsilon$, or an allocated factor $C_i$ satisfying $$\mu_i\ge b_\eta\epsilon,
\qquad
4\Delta_i\le\min\{k,\mu_i(p+1)\}.$$

nodes.label: Factor-local cleanup leaves a lifting seed
nodes.notes: In the factor branch, use $|E_i|\ge k|T_i|$, $\gamma_i\le\Delta_i$, $\Xi_i\le\Delta_i^2/d$, and $d>100$. The displayed factor bounds then leave enough clean edges for averaging.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under AE-17 and the factor alternative of AE-19, delete every identically $C_{i,Z}$-ramified line and every incidence $(x,L)$ with $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))=0$. The remaining factor-class edge set $E_i^{\mathrm{cl}}$ satisfies $$|E_i^{\mathrm{cl}}|>p^2\Delta_i.$$ In the polynomial alternative, retain its stated conclusion.

nodes.label: Vinh-free lifting and global aggregation
nodes.notes: Average the clean edges to obtain one point with more than $\Delta_i$ factor-consistent directions. Formalize the Newton step from the accepted propagation proof, then use irreducibility and edge-to-point double counting. No component-size estimate is needed.
nodes.statement_markdown: The alternatives in AE-20 imply that there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ with $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge b_\eta\epsilon.$$ In the factor alternative, the conclusion follows with $C_i$ associated to $Z-Q$ and $$\Pr[Q=f]\ge\mu_i.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear algebraic propagation engine
nodes.notes: No corpus submission proves this theorem. It remains blocked on AE-18, AE-19, the pending audit behind AE-17, and formalization of AE-20--AE-21.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $0<\eta<1$ there are constants $C_\eta,c_\eta,a_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every line-versus-point instance whose accepted graph contains an $(\epsilon,a_\eta)$-core, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac d p\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

summary: The exact accepted corpus supplies a complete component-level chain from reaching-family selection through weighted interpolation, linewise extension, characteristic-safe cleanup, vertical simplicity, and recovery of one polynomial. Its whole-explainer budgets force a square-root floor, while the audited universal-cover example and provisional uniform-jet calculation rule out two naive improvements. The shortest credible near-linear route is therefore: prove an algebraic-rank-or-decode dichotomy producing a low-weight relation on constant accepted mass; localize constant mass on one low-weight factor or decode cross-factor transitions; apply factorwise polar cleanup; and lift at one high-degree seed point. Once the irreducible factor is $Z-Q$, all of its assigned edges aggregate globally, avoiding both component fragmentation and the $p^{-1/2}$ mixing floor. The rank and heavy-factor nodes remain open, the factorwise polar input is pending audit, and the final theorem is blocked.
target_statement: Prove an algebraic interpolation-and-propagation lemma strong enough to preserve a near-linear power of the accepted incidence density over $\mathbb F_p^2$.
title: Algebraic propagation engine
